title: Finite modules admit a finitely presented approximation with stable closed fibre
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, meaning an integral domain whose fraction field $K$ has $a\in A$ or $a^{-1}\in A$ for every $a\in K^\times$; it is a local ring, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$. Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of local rings ($\mathfrak m_A$ is the inverse image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ of $B$) which is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], and let $N$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. There is a filtered system of finitely presented $B$-modules $N_\lambda$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] with surjective transition maps and colimit $N$ such that, for all sufficiently large $\lambda$, the map $N_\lambda/\mathfrak m_A N_\lambda\to N/\mathfrak m_A N$ induced by the colimit map $N_\lambda\to N$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: By finite generation [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], choose generators $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ and let $p:B^r\to N$ send the standard basis to them. Put $K=\ker p$. Index by the set $I$ of finite subsets $S\subset K$, ordered by inclusion; it is nonempty and directed because $S\cup T$ bounds $S,T$. Write $K_S=\langle S\rangle_B$ and $N_S=B^r/K_S$. The generators in $S$ give an exact sequence $B^{|S|}\to B^r\to N_S\to0$, so $N_S$ is finitely presented by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. For $S\subset T$ use the canonical quotient map $N_S\to N_T$, which is surjective.

The maps $N_S\to N$ have colimit $N$: given a compatible family $N_S\to X$, compose with $B^r\to N_S$. The resulting maps $B^r\to X$ are all equal, by compatibility with a common upper bound, and kill each $k\in K$ by using the stage $S=\{k\}$. Thus their common map factors uniquely through $B^r/K=N$. Conversely any map $N\to X$ gives that family. This is the colimit universal property, and the factorization is $B$-linear because all maps used are $B$-linear.
Put $J=\mathfrak m_A B$ and $R=B/J$. By [lem-trf-valuation-closed-fibre-noetherian], $R$ is Noetherian.

The induced surjection $\bar p:R^r\to N/JN$ is a map between finite $R$-modules: the standard basis generates $R^r$ and its images generate $N/JN$. Since $R$ is Noetherian by Step 3, [lem-pc-noetherian-finite-kernels-cokernels] shows that $L=\ker\bar p$ is a finite $R$-module.

The submodule $L$ is exactly the image of $K$ in $R^r$. One inclusion follows from $p(K)=0$. For the other, lift $x\in L$ to $v\in B^r$. Then $p(v)\in JN$, so $p(v)=\sum_a j_a y_a$ with $j_a\in J$ and $y_a\in N$. Choose lifts $w_a\in B^r$ of the finitely many $y_a$. The vector $v-\sum_a j_a w_a$ lies in $K$ and reduces to $x$. Choose finitely many generators $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t$ of $L$ and lifts $k_1,\ldots,k_t\in K$, and set $S_0=\{k_1,\ldots,k_t\}$. For every $S\supset S_0$, the image of $K_S$ in $R^r$ equals $L$: it contains the generators $\ell_a$ and is contained in the image of $K$.

For every finite $S\subset K$, both $(B^r/K_S)/J(B^r/K_S)$ and $R^r/\operatorname{im}(K_S\to R^r)$ are the quotient of $B^r$ by $K_S+JB^r$: in each case two vectors represent the same element precisely when their difference lies in this sum. Likewise $N/JN$ is the quotient of $B^r$ by $K+JB^r$, hence is $R^r/L$. If $S\supset S_0$, Step 5 identifies the two relation submodules in $R^r$, so the canonical map $N_S/JN_S\to N/JN$ is an isomorphism. Since $JN_S=\mathfrak m_A N_S$ and $JN=\mathfrak m_A N$ by the definition of the extended ideal $J$, this is the required eventual closed-fibre isomorphism.
